The Star of the Republic Museum was created by the Texas Legislature and is administered by the Texas Historical Commission as a cultural and educational institution. Its purpose is to collect and preserve the material culture of the Texas Republic (1836-1846) and to interpret the history, cultures, and values of early Texans.
See Washington-on-the-Brazos Complex
Plan Your Visit
A visit to the museum provides an overview of the Texas Republic period, beginning with a thirty-minute film entitled, Independence: A Lone Star Rises.
Star of the Republic Museum History
In 1965, Gus Mutscher, a state representative from Washington County, introduced a bill appropriating $800,000 for a “Worthy Museum, at the Birthplace of Texas that would be a Star upon a Star.”

Travel back in time to 1850 and explore the original home of Dr. Anson Jones, the last President of the Republic of Texas. The Jones family lived at the farm for over a decade, building a successful cotton farm with enslaved labor after Texas joined the union. This living history farm is complete with period costumed interpreters using 19th century farming practices for planting, cultivating, harvesting, and working with livestock. Explore the sights and smells of farm life and experience the daily lives of those who came 150 years ago.

Butchering & Curing
Saturday 10 a.m. - 4 p.m.
Butchering livestock was a very necessary way of life in the mid-19th century. The main source of meat, pork, has been preserved by drying, salting and smoking for centuries. Join us at Barrington Living History Farm for our annual butchering and curing weekend, where we will be butchering a hog on Saturday and beginning the curing process. This program will be ongoing, so if you wish to see every step, you must attend the entire event. Program is dependent on cool weather. For more information, please contact Ben Baumgartner at ben.baumgartner@thc.texas.gov, or 936-878-2214 ext. 248
